card.title: 62. INFANTRY REGIMENT

card.flavorText: The 62nd Infantry Regiment was a regiment belonging to the 7th Infantry Division of the German Wehrmacht during WWII. In 1939 the division was stationed in the Slovak Republic in preparation for the Invasion of Poland. In 1940, it took part in the Battle of France, where it saw action across Belgium and northern France. In June 1941, the 7th Infantry Division joined Operation Barbarossa as part of Army Group North in its push towards Leningrad, but it was later attached to Army Group Center in defensive operations. Over time, the division suffered heavy losses due to continuous Soviet attacks and the harsh winter conditions, but it remained engaged in defensive and retreat actions as German forces were pushed westward. In 1944–45, the division was involved in rear-guard actions as the Soviet Army advanced through Eastern Europe. During the Soviet summer offensive of 1944, the division narrowly escaped destruction when Army Group Center fell apart. It retreated through Poland to the Vistula River line. In January 1945, Soviet forces cut it off during their winter offensive, isolating the division on the Hel Peninsula near Danzig. The division surrendered there on May 8th, 1945.
